data.name: Garuda
data.gender_notes: Garuda is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Hindu mythology, Garuda is the king of birds and the vehicle of Lord Vishnu. He is depicted as a powerful and wise being with the ability to fly at great speeds. Garuda is also considered the protector of Lord Vishnu and is believed to have the power to free devotees from their suffering. The name Garuda carries the meaning “Eagle-like being” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Garuda usually hope their child will grow to embody eagle-like being and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Garuda belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Eagle-like being.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Garuda total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: Garuda is an integral part of Hindu mythology, particularly associated with Lord Vishnu and his avatars. He is depicted as a mighty and swift mythological bird with distinct traits such as sharp talons, eagle eyes, and a serpentine hood. In ancient Indian art, Garuda often appears as a dynamic and fierce symbol of power and freedom. Additionally, the iconography of Garuda plays an essential role in Hindu temples and religious festivities – for instance, in the famous Konark Sun Temple in Odisha, India, Garuda is a prominent feature.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hindu mythology, Garuda holds deep spiritual significance as the vehicle of Lord Vishnu, the preserver of the universe, in his various forms. The bird is revered not only as a powerful mythological creature, but also as a symbol of protection, freedom, and spiritual progression. Moreover, in Hindu scriptures like the Mahabharata and the Puranas, there are numerous tales that illustrate Garuda's wisdom, courage, and benevolence – for example, he saves Lord Vishnu's consort, Lakshmi, and their oft-stolen elephant, Airavata, from captivity; and he provides chosen mortals with the spiritual knowledge that helps them attain liberation. Thus, for Hindus, Garuda represents the infinite wisdom, boundless power, and compassionate protection that are integral aspects of their faith.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Garuda, the divine bird-king, symbolizes freedom, power, and wisdom. His swiftness and strength represent the triumph of knowledge and spirit over physical constraints. As Vishnu's mount, he embodies the transcendence of earthly limitations and the soaring heights of enlightenment.

historical_references.reference: Garuda is mentioned in the ancient Indian epic Mahabharata, where he is described as the mount of the god Vishnu and the god of wind, the storm, and the eagle.

Garuda is also depicted in ancient Hindu art, particularly in rock-cut architecture and sculpture, as a winged creature with the body of a man, the head and wings of an eagle, and the importance of the vehicle of the god Vishnu and the sun god Surya.

modern_usage.modern_context: The mythological bird Garuda, known as the mount and vehicle of the Hindu god Vishnu, has been adopted in various modern contexts. In Hindu mythology, Garuda symbolizes freedom, strength, and the power of flight. In the air travel industry, Garuda Indonesia is the national airline of Indonesia, named after this mythological bird. In the technology sector, Garuda is the name of an intelligent autonomous agent in AI technology, designed for search and retrieval of data. This intelligent agent, also known as a 'Garuda bot', uses machine learning algorithms to efficiently search and retrieve data, demonstrating the power and freedom of flight in the digital world.

name_in_real_life.story: Radha Garuda, a teacher in Hyderabad, India, shares that their name Garuda meaning "Eagle-like being" has been a constant source of inspiration, motivating them to follow Hindu values and serve their community.
